relations.myth: Shu forms the primordial Eight from his emanation
relations.note: Shu fashions or organizes the Eight from his emanation or limbs.

relations.myth: The Eight support Shu and the celestial structure
relations.note: At Shu's command, the Eight support him and the celestial ladder.

relations.myth: Primordial powers enter the Atum-Shu creation sequence
relations.note: The Eight or related chaos-powers appear within the creation sequence preceding Shu.

relations.myth: The Eight produce the local solar creator Atum
relations.note: Some later temple systems make the Eight precede or produce Atum.
Nun is both an Ogdoad member and the encompassing primeval water.

relations.myth: The Eight bring forth the first sun
relations.note: The Eight generate or reveal Re as the newborn solar creator.

relations.myth: The Eight acclaim the first sunrise
relations.note: The Eight protect, worship, and greet the newborn sun, sometimes as baboons.

relations.myth: Re-Horakhty emerges from the egg or lotus
relations.note: A regional version makes Re-Horakhty the solar child produced by the Eight.

relations.myth: Shepsi appears as the child of the Eight
relations.note: The local Hermopolitan solar god replaces Re as child of the Eight.

relations.myth: Nefertum appears as the lotus-born solar child
relations.note: One regional lotus version names Nefertum as the emerging solar child.

relations.myth: The Eight join Thoth in praising Merenptah
relations.note: At Hermopolis, the Eight appear beside Thoth and join his royal praise.

relations.myth: Thoth presides beside the Hermopolitan Eight
relations.note: Later local theology associates the city's principal god with its primordial company.

relations.myth: Amun manifests his hidden unity as the Eight
relations.note: The entire Ogdoad is interpreted as the first plural manifestation of Amun.
Amun is also one member of the standard four-pair roster.
Amaunet is Amun's female counterpart and a member of the standard roster.

relations.myth: Ogdoadic powers become forms of Ptah
relations.note: Nun and Naunet are treated as Ptah forms under his creative priority.

relations.myth: The Eight accompany the primordial mound's manifestation
relations.note: Amun-Ptah-Tatenen is linked with the Eight as first manifestation and divine source.

relations.myth: Kematef precedes the Eight in Theban creation
relations.note: Theban theology presents Kematef as a primordial ancestor or generator of the Eight.

relations.myth: Kematef and the Eight rest at Djeme
relations.note: The primeval serpent rests with the completed creator-gods at their sacred necropolis.

relations.myth: Irta generates the Eight in Theban cosmogony
relations.note: A later Theban creator form connects Kematef to the Eight and living Amun.

relations.myth: Amenope renews the buried Eight at Djeme
relations.note: Amenope visits every ten days and pours libations for the ancestor gods.

relations.myth: The dead Eight follow an Osirian regeneration pattern
relations.note: The Eight's burial, offerings, and renewal at Djeme are assimilated to Osirian theology.

relations.myth: The Eight adore Hathor's solar manifestation
relations.note: Dendera's creator theology shows the Eight worshipping Hathor or her solar form.

relations.myth: Khonsu's creator form generates the Eight
relations.note: Ptolemaic Theban theology makes a creator form of Khonsu generate or encompass them.

relations.myth: Neith precedes parallel companies of dead creator-gods
relations.note: Esna places Neith before creator gods but does not universally parent the standard Eight.

relations.myth: An Ogdoad-like company enters Horus's primordial prehistory
relations.note: Edfu appropriates an Ogdoad-like group into its local falcon god's creation theology.

relations.myth: The Eight join processions serving the local goddess
relations.note: Philae and Dendera place the Eight in cosmogonic sequences serving Isis.

relations.myth: The Eight sustain the cosmos after earth separates
relations.note: The Eight support the differentiated cosmos after Shu separates Geb from Nut.

relations.myth: The Eight sustain the cosmos after sky separates
relations.note: The Eight support the differentiated cosmos after Shu separates Nut from Geb.
